LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 3.1.1 PRONUNCIATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.1: Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation, part of Strand 3 in Grade 9 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How can we tell the difference between one indigenous language and another? 2. Why should we take part in community service?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers to identify words that are commonly mispronounced,

2. list the words on a chart and display them in class,

3. conduct a gallery walk to read the words in turns,

4. read words displayed on flashcards using correct intonation,

5. watch a pre-recorded audio clip on the theme and identify the vocabulary used,

6. prepare a short talk on community service using correct intonation and accentuation,

7. present the talk to peers for review, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to identify words that are commonly mispronounced,
2. list the words on a chart and display them in class,
3. conduct a gallery walk to read the words in turns,
4. read words displayed on flashcards using correct intonation,
5. watch a pre-recorded audio clip on the theme and identify the vocabulary used,
6. prepare a short talk on community service using correct intonation and accentuation,
7. present the talk to peers for review, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner contributes to group decision-making when working with peers to identify

words that are commonly mispronounced.

• Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner plans and manages time effectively to prepare and present a short talk

on serving the community using correct intonation and accentuation.

Values:
• Respect: This is enhanced as the learner appreciates diverse opinions when holding a discussion forum on instances in

which wrong intonation on words affects meaning implied in a language.

• Unity: It is promoted as the learner appreciates the effort of those who present the short talk to peers during review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Civic Responsibility: It is promoted as the learner discusses content from the theme on how to embrace serving the

community for nation building.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of pronunciation to the concepts of stress and intonation in English and Kiswahili.
